thirdParty.$comment: No analytics collector is configured on this site (site.json trackingIds is empty, no lilstts SDK). Every third-party browser request is replayed from the per-case HAR; `block` stays available for beacons.

decoEventsRecorder.$comment: The analytics contract here is window.DECO.events.dispatch (ANALYTICS_SCRIPT data-event observers, the search form's `search` event). parity/lib/capture.mjs wraps dispatch from an init script and every call lands in the snapshot's `analytics.events`.

$volatileHarMissesComment: Harness noise, NOT approvals, and reported as PENDING whenever one changes a result (--strict fails then). Entries are full request URLs: the home's mobile <source> images (Hero slides and the Banner, the `-mob` files), only on desktop captures. Chromium's full-page capture (captureBeyondViewport) sometimes re-runs <picture> source selection against a transient narrow frame, so those images are requested and aborted on some captures of the same build and not on others: v7 requested all four on every capture so far (the baseline, v7-self runs), one v8 build went pass, pass, fail in a row. Dropped from harMisses on both sides for the listed cases; pixels and thirdPartyRequests still compare. PARITY_DEBUG_MISSES=1 prints every aborted URL.

The HARs were recorded on v7, which never requested them, so they are listed under harMisses.

$pendingBaselinesComment: NOT approvals. A pendingBaselines rule covers cases whose whole page differs from v7 for an explained reason the product owner hasn't signed off: compare checks those cases against the v8 capture pinned in `dir` (node parity/run.mjs record-pending --rule <id>, which records the upstream/HAR fixtures v7 never needed into that dir) and reports them PENDING, never ok; --strict fails on them; --no-pending compares them with the v7 baseline instead. `dir`/README.md lists how each case differs from v7. Only the product owner signs one off; an agent only adds them.

pendingBaselines.reason: PENDING product-owner approval (not approved). On v7 the Shopify listing loader never got the page URL (it fell back to https://localhost), so every category, search, catch-all and /sitemap.xml page asked Shopify for the collection "" and showed "12 of 0" results, live too. v8 passes the page URL: the breadcrumb names the collection or the query, the listing JSON-LD carries the collection's title and description, and the page lists the collection's products. The store's catalog was replaced on 2026-10-10 (its old collections are empty now), so the capture pinned here, recorded after that, shows today's empty collections: identical to v7 except the breadcrumb and the JSON-LD. parity/pending/listing-live-before-catalog-change/ has v8 captured live on 2026-10-09, before the change, listing the products (7 shirts, filters, sort).

pages.$comment: v7 has no sitemap: /sitemap.xml is served by the /* catch-all Category page (200 HTML). Parity reproduces that page.

flows.blocked: v7 live bug (main 928488a and https://demo-storefront.deco-cx.workers.dev/ alike): every PLP and search page renders '12 of 0 results' with no products, no filters and no pagination, so this flow cannot run on v7. The breadcrumb/view_item_list item_list_id is '/', i.e. the Shopify PLP loader resolves the page URL to '/' and queries an empty collection handle. Not run, not compared; decision for the product owner (fix on v8 = a product change, reported as PENDING).

flows.$comment: The card is scrolled into view and the page settled BEFORE the click, so the shelf's view_item_list (IntersectionObserver) always fires on '/', never racing the SPA navigation.

$fixedTimeNote: Must be in the FUTURE relative to the wall clock: the server clock is frozen to it and cookies (cart, 7-day expiry) are dated from it, while Chromium's cookie jar uses real time. Re-record before 2030-01-08.
$approvalsComment: Approvals are PER SITE. This harness was ported from storefront-tanstack, whose product-owner approvals do NOT carry over: this site starts with none. Only the product owner adds entries here (ignoreHeaders / approvedDifferences, see parity/README.md); an agent never does.
